opportunities.gap: The recurring privacy boundary clause ('without exposing names to a third party', 'data handling', 'sending names off-site') appears across the Opening Case, Worked Example, Decision Rule, parameter-explorer, and Final Check, yet no privacy statute is cited. opportunities.proposed_change: Add a 2-3 sentence 'Why the boundary is legal, not just preferential' note after Decision Rule item 3 (Boundary check), naming FERPA and COPPA as statutory backing. FERPA: disclosing personally identifiable information (PII) from education records to a third party generally requires prior written consent (34 CFR 99.30); the school-official/contractor exception (34 CFR 99.31) lets a vendor receive PII ONLY for the contracted purpose and bars re-disclosure without consent, so 'sending names off-site' is a consent-bound act, not a preference. COPPA: under the FTC's amended Rule (published Jan 2025, effective June 23, 2025, full compliance by April 22, 2026), operators collecting from under-13 students must obtain verifiable parental consent before disclosing data to third parties or using it for targeted advertising, and may not retain children's data indefinitely (only as long as reasonably necessary). Add matching citations to References.

sources.cite: U.S. DoE, FERPA regulations, 34 CFR 99.30 (prior consent required) and 99.31 (exceptions, incl. school-official/contractor)
sources.finding: A parent/eligible student must give signed written consent before an agency discloses PII from education records (99.30); the contractor/service-provider exception (99.31) permits a vendor to receive PII only for the purpose disclosed and forbids re-disclosure without consent. Grounds 'without exposing names to a third party' as a statutory line, not a preference.

sources.cite: FTC (Jan 2025) Final Rule amending the Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule (COPPA)
sources.finding: Amended COPPA Rule (effective June 23, 2025; full-compliance deadline April 22, 2026) requires separate verifiable parental consent before disclosing under-13 children's data to third parties or using it for targeted ads, and bars indefinite data retention (retain only as long as reasonably necessary). Note: FTC did NOT finalize the proposed ed-tech-specific amendments, continuing to enforce COPPA in ed tech under existing guidance — so cite COPPA's general third-party-disclosure/retention provisions, not a new ed-tech rule.

sources.cite: FTC (2025), Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule — Final Amendments
sources.finding: First major COPPA update since 2013: effective June 23, 2025, full compliance by April 22, 2026. Requires SEPARATE verifiable parental consent before disclosing a child's personal information to third parties for targeted advertising; bars indefinite data retention (retain only as long as reasonably necessary); expands 'personal information' to include biometric and government identifiers — a concrete late data-handling gate for under-13 students.

sources.cite: U.S. Dept. of Education, Student Privacy Policy Office — Responsibilities of Third-Party Service Providers under FERPA
sources.finding: Under FERPA (20 U.S.C. 1232g) the 'school official' exception lets a district share education records with an edtech vendor without parental consent only if the vendor performs an institutional service, has a legitimate educational interest, is under the school's direct control via contract, and is barred from further disclosure — a concrete data-handling constraint a vendor's account/data-sharing model can trip.
